objects.question: What is the whole thing for, and what settles it?
objects.notes: Goal, acceptance criteria, instructions, status, optional coordinator session. Completion is derived from its criteria, requested by the coordinator and recorded by the owner.

objects.question: What is the one piece of work?
objects.notes: One durable work item with exactly one completion criterion. A task may be filed under a project, a list, a parent and prerequisites, but none of those is what it is.

objects.question: How is this class of work dispatched?
objects.notes: Dispatch policy: maxConcurrent, paused (dispatch hold), standing instructions, and the queue task priority orders. It decides when work may run, never what the work is.

objects.question: What is running right now?
objects.notes: One engine conversation on a runner, task-linked or standalone. A session can end; the task outlives it.

objects.question: Where does it run, and under which identity?
objects.notes: Execution identity and location. In the live product this is the workspace row named by MCP agent_* and CLI orbit agent; project-agent-contract.md freezes a future pure-identity split.

routingRules.rule: The smaller object wins: one task beats a project; one task beats a batch of one.
Never double-record: not a task per step of the current task, not a task for the current task, not a session to do what this turn can do.
Read before write when the destination is uncertain: task_list --project-id, project_get, or task_create_batch dryRun.
An engine plan/todo is private scratch; never call it an Orbit record, never claim a task without its id, never refuse to record work because a private plan covers it.

mcp.resultShape: since 1.3.0 every catalogued write answers with the versioned receipt (receipt.schema) as structuredContent and as its text, as does a call refused before it ran; a read keeps its text and carries the receipt as structuredContent when it answered with a JSON document or failed, a read answered in prose keeps its text alone; the wiki tools keep their own outputSchema and permission_prompt the engine's protocol
mcp.engineView: measured 2026-11-13, Claude Code 2.1.325: a successful result's structuredContent reaches the model as compact JSON in place of its text; an error result's text is shown as it is; Codex prefers structuredContent likewise
mcp.outputSchema: the receipt schema, advertised on task_create, task_create_batch, task_update, task_start, project_create, project_update, tasklist_create, tasklist_update, session_create, agent_create, agent_update

guide.index: the five objects, the intent routes R1.1-R1.14 (object, operations, topic, availability and reason) and the routing rules R2-R5, held to objects, intentRoutes and routingRules here
guide.topic: one topic's shortest recipe: per step the MCP tool and absolute CLI argv, availability on each surface with the reason, mutates, approval and approvalKey, a minimal example on both surfaces and successEvidence; then the rules that span the tools and what proves the topic done

mcp.unknownArguments: since 1.3.0 refused before any request with INVALID_ARGUMENTS, naming the field; every object that names its properties is advertised additionalProperties:false (permission_prompt stays open)

useFor: work that must outlive the turn
cli.capabilities: orbit capabilities --json (schemaVersion 2; context-dependent). Since 1.1.0 each entry also carries object, intent, risk, approval/approvalKey/approvalDetail, destructive, idempotency, retry, successEvidence, nextStep, returns and availability, and the document carries catalogVersion and catalogHash.

views.summary: orbit capabilities --summary --json: one row per offered command (id, intent; mutates and approval when not false/none) by family, plus unavailable and withheld groups each with its reason
views.family: orbit capabilities --family NAME --json: each command of one family with absolute argv, usage, available, mutates, risk, approval, successEvidence, nextStep and a minimal CLI example; reasons grouped under unavailable
views.id: orbit capabilities --id ID --json: one catalogued operation in full (MCP-only ones included) with description, leaf parameters, mutuallyExclusive, idempotency, retry, returns, availability, helpArgv and both surfaces' examples

gradedDiscovery.examples: generated from the catalogue: an MCP tool's required fields, a command's required arguments, filled from the row's Example or a <placeholder>; tests pass each through its own surface

cli.discoveryToday: since 1.6.0: the guide and graded views (gradedDiscovery); the task-create discovery measured 2026-11-14 at 6.0 KB (guide index) + 5.8 KB (guide task-create) + 6.8 KB (capabilities --id task_create) = 18.6 KB with a 60-character executable path, against 319 KB for the whole document in the fullest context
cli.jsonOutput: entity document on stdout only (the receipt's entity); hints on stderr
cli.receiptOutput: --receipt on any catalogued command: the receipt on stdout only, a failure's included; exit 0 exactly when ok; the capabilities document names it as receiptFlag
cli.jsonPayloads: since 1.3.0 a --tasks document is judged against task_create_batch's schema (closed items, types, required fields, exclusive pairs) before any card or request
cli.unknownFlags: refused with exit 1 before any request

writeAuthority.machineCredential: the agent's credential: task create, create-batch and DAG apply require a usable acting session (this runner's, this account's, not ended) and an ALLOWED card covering the exact write; there is no session-less form — x-orbit-session-id is attribution, so an agent can unset it (v1.2.0)
writeAuthority.personCredential: the owner's own act: orbit login or ORBIT_USER_TOKEN writes task create and create-batch on /api/tasks card-free by design; a person's terminal edits DAG edges one at a time, and the batch restructure has no person route (v1.2.0)

parity.note: Since 1.1.0 the operation catalogue (src/runner-go/operation_catalog.go) is the single declaration; these are its current declared gaps, each with a reason in the catalogue row.

permission.today: the runner adds no permission-mode gate of its own; the engines differ: Codex plan refuses every MCP call, Codex default/acceptEdits cards every MCP call, Claude's plan policy is unmeasured
permission.target: plan allows Orbit reads and refuses Orbit writes (P1-02)

orchestration.revocation: immediate on session end/reassign or switch off

permission.attribution: in-session writes go to the session's agent and are linked to the session; headless writes fall back to the runner owner

retry.serverInternal: task create runs in one transaction retried on transient database conflict; a redelivered turn dedups on a turn-derived key
retry.createWithoutKey: sent exactly once; a lost answer's receipt says outcome unknown, retry reread_first: re-read before retrying; a retry in a later turn does not dedup
retry.createWithKey: the runner resends it under the same key while the answer is lost (up to 3 resends); the server answers a repeat with the first write in any turn; the same key with a different title or description is refused 409

receiptRetryRules.resend: the same call unchanged is safe and may succeed; error.retryable is true exactly for this
receiptRetryRules.reread_first: the outcome is unknown or conflicted: re-read, then decide
receiptRetryRules.do_not_retry: a boundary or a person's no: report it
receiptRetryRules.wait: a person has not answered yet

errors.unknownFields: since 1.3.0 refused before any network write with INVALID_ARGUMENTS, every violation as {path, problem, message} (G1 satisfied)

shape.message: the human rejected this task: why
shape.decidedBy: user id, absent when no person answered

receipts.write: card answered with Chat about this
required: text: the owner's message as ownerChatReply writes it
receipts.note: since 1.4.0: not a refusal. Nothing was written and the proposal is still open: answer the owner's message, then call again, changed as agreed. The MCP result is not marked isError and its text is that same reply; the CLI exits non-zero with it as the error

receiptRules: Read back when the claim matters.
A receipt is a document, not prose about it: read ok, outcome and id from it.
A decline is a refusal, not a success: outcome declined, APPROVAL_DECLINED, on both surfaces.
A chat is neither: outcome chat means the owner pressed Chat about this; reply to their words (approval.message), then ask again, changed as agreed.
Evidence is its own envelope (task_evidence_submit); a comment is not evidence and evidence is not a status write.

schema.description: The Orbit receipt (docs/orbit-agent-contract.md §6): ok and outcome say what happened; id and status are the entity's; error says why not and whether a resend is safe.
schema.title: OrbitReceiptV1

scenarios.baselineNote: since 1.3.0, contract-tested, not black-box measured; was PARTIAL
scenarios.baselineEvidence: tool + card exist; the answer is the receipt with the task's id (G1/G3 closed by P0-04); a decline is the shared APPROVAL_DECLINED outcome (G4 closed by P0-03, carried by the receipt since 1.3.0)

scenarios.name: Private plan
scenarios.baselineEvidence: primer states the rule; no enforcement; plan-mode write gate not implemented (G9)

scenarios.name: Create without start
scenarios.baselineEvidence: the separation exists (startNow/runAt/autoRunWhenReady/card override); autoRunWhenReady defaults to true, so no-start requires an explicit false; since 1.5.0 the primer and the create tools' descriptions lead with it (G11 closed); agent behaviour not black-box measured (P2-01)

scenarios.name: Batch plan
scenarios.baselineNote: since 1.3.0, contract-tested, not black-box measured; was PARTIAL
scenarios.baselineEvidence: dry-run receipt measured; atomic refs; a real write's receipt maps every item (items, count); since v1.2.0 the server refuses a session batch no answered card covers; a decline is outcome declined

scenarios.name: Read-only project inspection
scenarios.baselineEvidence: project_get measured; no project list surface (G6)

scenarios.name: Immediate delegation
scenarios.baselineEvidence: task_start/session_create semantics hold; since 1.3.0 the create's receipt carries the start (G3 closed); decline is one document (G4 closed by P0-03)

scenarios.name: No orchestration
scenarios.baselineNote: code-inspected since 1.5.0; agent behaviour not black-box measured (P2-01)
scenarios.baselineEvidence: 22 tools disappear (measured); since 1.5.0 the primer says what to do when the family is absent

scenarios.name: Compaction recovery
scenarios.baselineEvidence: Codex re-injects after compaction; Claude keeps the system prompt; since 1.5.0 the primer is the MCP initialize instructions, Claude Code 2.1.325 still quoted it after a manual /compact (measured 2026-11-14), and every Codex mode is tested to carry it after compaction and resume; no black-box test of the scenario (G10)

gaps.gap: unknown MCP fields and wrong types silently ignored
gaps.resolution: every catalogued tool call is judged against its advertised closed schema and the catalogue's exclusive groups before any request; the CLI judges --tasks the same way

gaps.note: initialize answers with the versioned agent primer; every engine's injected instructions open with the same text

gaps.gap: write receipts are unversioned text; start outcome split; no structuredContent
gaps.resolution: the versioned receipt is every tool's structuredContent and every write's text; the five objects' creates/updates and task_start advertise it as outputSchema; --receipt prints it at the CLI

gaps.gap: declined card is a non-error MCP result and a non-zero CLI error
gaps.owner: P0-03 (closed); P0-04 for the remaining receipt format
gaps.note: both surfaces return the same APPROVAL_DECLINED document; the transport difference (tool result vs non-zero exit) is the surface's, not the outcome's. Since 1.3.0 (P0-04) that outcome is the receipt's: outcome declined, error.code APPROVAL_DECLINED, approval.decision and decidedBy, on MCP and on --receipt

gaps.gap: task creates take no caller idempotency key
gaps.resolution: task_create and task_create_batch take idempotencyKey (session-scoped; the account's for a person's own create); the runner resends a keyed create whose answer was lost

gaps.gap: no project list surface on either agent surface
gaps.resolution: recorded as a deliberate absence in the operation catalogue; since 1.6.0 the guide's inspect topic says where a project id comes from, and the list stays absent

gaps.gap: one 255 KB capabilities document; no graded discovery
gaps.resolution: the always-listed read-only guide tool and orbit guide [topic] answer the intent routes and one topic's recipe; orbit capabilities --summary/--family/--id answer the catalogue a view at a time with context, absolute argv, availability and reason, mutates/approval, a generated minimal example and success evidence; every graded answer is at most 16 KiB and the task-create discovery 24 KiB; the whole document is unchanged

gaps.gap: MCP and CLI surfaces differ by 14 and 3 operations; no single operation catalogue
gaps.resolution: operation_catalog.go declares every operation once; tools/list and capabilities are projections; every deliberate one-surface gap carries a reason; a mandatory test executes every advertised argv/helpArgv

gaps.gap: permission-mode behaviour for Orbit calls is not uniform: no runner gate; Codex plan refuses all MCP calls, Codex default/acceptEdits cards every MCP call, Claude plan policy unmeasured
no black-box evaluation for the eight scenarios
autoRunWhenReady defaults to true and the create tool's top-level description does not lead with it: file-it-for-later can start work once the project starts unless the agent passes false
gaps.note: the primer's first paragraph and the create tools' descriptions on both surfaces lead with the default; the default stays true
